title: Questionnaire response automation and contract cliffnotes
creator: Avery Johnson
description: Deliver an automated pipeline that turns incoming customer security questionnaires (SIG/CAIQ and vendor-specific forms) into a draft response bundle plus a one-page "cliffnotes" summary for sales and legal. Tie the output to a small pricing/entitlement decision matrix so that certain questionnaire outcomes trigger predefined commercial guardrails (e.g., required Dedicated deployment, enhanced logging add-on, or SSO requirement). Goal: reduce manual effort for questionnaires by ~80% and standardize pricing triggers for commonly requested controls.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest CAIQ and a common subset of vendor forms and produce a pre-filled response JSON for review
Generate a one-page PDF ‘contract cliffnotes’ that highlights commitments impacting pricing or delivery (data residency, isolation, SLAs, audit support)
Implement a ruleset that maps specific questionnaire answers to pricing/entitlement recommendations and surface as flags in the Console sales view
Automate creation of a draft Confluence evidence page and a GitHub PR that contains the proposed answers and supporting links
Security review checklist completed and sign-off from Security Org for final templates
tasks: Define canonical question->answer mappings for CAIQ common sections (Data Protection, Access Control, Infrastructure)
Build a lightweight parser to map incoming spreadsheets/PDFs to canonical question keys (ENG-20234)
Create Jinja-like templates for canned answers and variable placeholders (e.g., Customer-managed keys => yes/no)
Design one-page 'cliffnotes' layout and content prioritized for Sales and Legal (DES-904)
Prototype a decision matrix service that outputs recommended pricing flags and rationale
Wire Console sales panel to show flags and attach generated artifacts
Run 3 pilot questionnaires with Sales and measure time to first-draft and review cycles
decisions: Use CAIQ 'essential' subset as the initial surface area to limit scope
Answers will default to 'Redwood standard' where possible with opt-outs for bespoke contracts
Pricing flags are advisory by default and require Sales/Legal confirmation before being enforced
Generated artifacts will be stored in a dedicated Confluence space and linked into the Console
Leverage existing KMS integration work rather than reimplementing key management text for each questionnaire
